title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Program Limits on Loan-to-Value, Term, Direct Loan Rate and Trust Land
content:
Each program of the VA Home Loan Guaranty sets its own maximum loan amount as a percent of the reasonable value (before a financed funding fee), its longest loan term, the interest rate VA charges on a Native American Direct Loan (0.00 percent for lender-made loans), and whether the home must be on federal trust land.

## Limits by program

| Program | Maximum loan amount (% of reasonable value, before the financed funding fee) | Longest term (years) | VA interest rate (% a year) | Home must be on federal trust land |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) | 100 | 30 | 0.00 | No |
| VA Manufactured Home Loan | 95 | 20 | 0.00 | No |
| VA Purchase Loan (10% or More Down) | 100 | 30 | 0.00 | No |
| VA Purchase Loan (5% to Less Than 10% Down) | 100 | 30 | 0.00 | No |
| VA Purchase Loan (Less Than 5% Down) | 100 | 30 | 0.00 | No |
| VA Cash-Out Refinance Loan | 100 | 30 | 0.00 | No |
| Native American Direct Loan (NADL) | 100 | 30 | 6.25 | Yes |

## Points of reading

- The VA Manufactured Home Loan is the only program with a maximum below 100 percent of the reasonable value (95) and a longest term below 30 years (20).
- The Native American Direct Loan (NADL) is the only program on which VA charges interest (6.25 percent a year) and the only one requiring federal trust land. On the lender-made programs the figure is 0.00.

## Hypothetical illustration

On a manufactured home with a hypothetical reasonable value of 120,000.00 dollars, the largest loan amount before any financed funding fee is 120,000.00 multiplied by 95 and divided by one hundred, or 114,000.00 dollars; under a program with the 100 percent limit the same value would support up to 120,000.00 dollars.
